```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
library(shokenuse)
```

shokenuse shows where your Claude Code tokens and cost go: by day, by project, by session, and by prompt. In this guide I'll cover how to launch the app, where its data comes from, and how the pieces fit together.

## Launching the app

`launch_app()` reads `~/.cache/token-metrics` by default. Pass `dir` to read another folder, or the example data that ships with the package:

```{r}
#| label: launch
library(shokenuse)

launch_app()                                  # reads ~/.cache/token-metrics
launch_app(dir = "/path/to/token-metrics")    # another folder

# Example data shipped with the package
launch_app(dir = system.file("extdata", "token-metrics", package = "shokenuse"))
```

The example data is made up: 7 days, 4 projects, and one expensive session on 2026-11-06.

## Where does the data come from?

The app never reads Claude Code's transcripts directly. `token-metrics.py` reads them from `~/.claude/projects/` every hour and writes one CSV per day, with one row per prompt. The app reads those CSVs. `vignette("token-metrics")` explains the script in detail.

```{mermaid}
%%| eval: true
%%| fig-height: 6
%%| fig-cap: 'Data pipeline'
%%{init: {'theme': 'base', 'themeVariables': { 'fontFamily': 'monospace', 'fontSize':'16px', 'darkMode':false}}}%%

flowchart TD
    cc(["<strong>Claude Code</strong>"]) --> tr[("transcripts<br/><code>~/.claude/projects/</code>")]
    tr --> py("<code>token-metrics.py</code><br/>hourly")
    py --> csv[("daily CSVs<br/><code>~/.cache/token-metrics/</code>")]
    csv --> rd[["<code>util_read_token_metrics()</code>"]]
    rd --> app(["<strong>shokenuse</strong><br/>Overview, By Project, Sessions, Prompts"])

    style py fill:#4CBB9D,color:#FFFFFF,rx:5,ry:5
    style rd fill:#4CBB9D,color:#FFFFFF
```

## Tabs

The app has five tabs. Each one has its own article:

| Tab | Description |
|---|---|
| Data | Folder path, reload, and upload; latest prompts. |
| Overview | Totals and daily tokens or cost by project. |
| By Project | Tokens and cost per project, with git remotes. |
| Sessions | One row per session, outliers flagged, CSV export. |
| Prompts | Search and rank prompts by tokens or cost. |

The sidebar date range and project filters apply to every tab after Data.

## Architecture

The diagram below shows how the modules share data. The Data module reads the folder and any uploads into one `metrics` reactive. The Filters module applies the sidebar filters to `metrics` and passes the result, `filtered`, to every tab module. Each tab module calls the `util_*` functions to summarise and plot.

```{mermaid}
%%| eval: true
%%| fig-height: 8
%%| fig-cap: 'Module and reactive flow'
%%{init: {'theme': 'base', 'themeVariables': { 'fontFamily': 'monospace', 'fontSize':'16px', 'darkMode':false}}}%%

flowchart TD
    launch(["<code>launch_app(dir)</code>"]) --> ui[["<code>app_ui()</code><br/>navbar, filters sidebar, tab UIs"]]
    launch --> data
    csv[("token-metrics folder")] --> data
    up[/"uploaded CSVs"/] --> data
    subgraph srv["<strong>app_server()</strong>"]
        data[["<code>mod_data_server()</code><br/>util_read_token_metrics()"]]
        filt[["<code>mod_filters_server()</code><br/>date range, projects"]]
        ov[["<code>mod_overview_server()</code><br/>util_plot_daily()"]]
        pr[["<code>mod_project_server()</code><br/>util_plot_rank()"]]
        se[["<code>mod_sessions_server()</code><br/>util_summarise_sessions()"]]
        po[["<code>mod_prompts_server()</code><br/>util_plot_prompts()"]]
        data -->|"metrics"| filt
        filt -->|"filtered"| ov
        filt -->|"filtered"| pr
        filt -->|"filtered"| se
        filt -->|"filtered"| po
    end

    style srv fill:#FFFFFF,color:#000000,stroke:#333,stroke-width:1px,rx:10,ry:10
    style data fill:#4CBB9D,color:#FFFFFF
    style filt fill:#4CBB9D,color:#FFFFFF
```

### Call stack

The call tree below is built with [`stackcallr`](https://mjfrigaard.github.io/stackcallr/). `call_tree_dir()` parses the files in `R/` without running them, so the tree always matches the code. It starts at `launch_app()` and follows every internal function down to the `util_*` helpers. The internal `%||%` operator is left out because it appears under most modules:

```{r}
#| label: call-stack
#| eval: !expr requireNamespace("stackcallr", quietly = TRUE)
#| collapse: false
#| comment: ""
stackcallr::call_tree_dir("../R", root = "launch_app", exclude = "%||%")
```

`util_metrics_dir()` is missing from the tree because it is only called as a default argument (`dir = util_metrics_dir()`), and `call_tree_dir()` reads function bodies, not their arguments.

## Using the functions without the app

The app's functions are exported, so you can run the same summaries in the console:

```{r}
#| label: utils
metrics <- util_read_token_metrics()

util_summarise_metrics(metrics, by = "day")
util_summarise_metrics(metrics, by = "project")
util_summarise_sessions(metrics)
```

## Changing the log level

shokenuse logs each file read and each read error at the `INFO` level. `util_log_threshold()` changes how much it logs:

```{r}
#| label: logging
util_log_threshold("DEBUG")   # more detail
util_log_threshold("OFF")     # silence
```
